summary: Hospital-based coordinator who runs a robotic surgery program: scheduling and turnover of systems like da Vinci, Hugo, Versius or Mako, staff training and credentialing, instrument-life and uptime tracking, vendor liaison, adverse-event reporting and program metrics. AI helps most with schedule and utilization analysis, drafting SOPs and credentialing files, structuring incident reviews and translating program data for surgeons, administrators and patients.

prompts.title: Weekly robot schedule optimizer
prompts.task: Balance robot allocation across services and rooms for the coming week
prompts.prompt: You are helping a surgical robot coordinator at a [HOSPITAL TYPE] with [NUMBER] robotic systems ([SYSTEM MODELS]) across [ROOMS]. Here is next week's case list with surgeon, procedure, estimated console time and room: [PASTE CASE LIST]. Constraints: [BLOCK TIME RULES, STAFF WITH ROBOT COMPETENCY BY DAY, SCHEDULED SERVICE/PM WINDOWS, INSTRUMENT SET COUNTS, REPROCESSING TURNAROUND]. Produce: (1) a day-by-day table assigning cases to systems and rooms, (2) a list of conflicts such as instrument set shortages, uncredentialed staff or tight turnovers, (3) two alternative fixes per conflict with trade-offs. State every assumption about turnover and docking times. Do not move cases between surgeons; flag those for human decision.
prompts.caution: Final schedule decisions stay with OR leadership; verify instrument and staffing data against your systems of record.

prompts.title: Utilization and cost dashboard narrative
prompts.task: Turn robot program data into a quarterly report for administration
prompts.prompt: Act as an analyst for a robotic surgery program. Using this de-identified quarterly data: [PASTE: cases by service, console and room time, turnover times, first-case on-time starts, conversions to open/lap, instrument uses and cost per case, system downtime]. Compare against our targets [TARGETS] and last quarter [PRIOR DATA]. Write a 1-page executive summary for the [CFO/PERIOPERATIVE COMMITTEE] with: key metrics table, three trends with likely drivers, cost-per-case drivers, and 3 recommended actions with expected impact. Clearly separate what the data shows from hypotheses, and list the data I'd need to confirm each hypothesis.
prompts.caution: Use de-identified aggregate data only; outcome comparisons need risk adjustment before drawing clinical conclusions.

prompts.title: Intraoperative fault troubleshooting log review
prompts.task: Analyze recurring system faults and prep a vendor escalation
prompts.prompt: I coordinate a [SYSTEM MODEL] program. Over the past [PERIOD] we logged these faults and interruptions (no patient identifiers): [PASTE: date, fault code/message, phase of case, arm/instrument involved, action taken, delay minutes]. Group them by likely category (instrument, arm/joint, vision, energy, console, network/software, user error), identify patterns by room, instrument lot or software version, and draft a concise escalation email to our [VENDOR] field service engineer requesting root-cause analysis. Include a list of questions to ask. Note where a pattern could be coincidence given the sample size. Do not suggest workarounds that bypass manufacturer safety interlocks or IFU.
prompts.caution: Never override device safety features; follow manufacturer IFU and your biomed department's procedures.

prompts.title: Adverse event and MDR triage memo
prompts.task: Structure an incident review and decide what reporting may apply
prompts.prompt: You are assisting a surgical robot coordinator with an event review. De-identified summary of what happened: [EVENT NARRATIVE, DEVICE/INSTRUMENT, LOT, PATIENT IMPACT, TIMELINE]. Produce: (1) a neutral factual timeline, (2) a contributing-factors analysis using a human-factors framework (device, user, team, environment, organization), (3) a checklist of reporting considerations in the US: FDA MedWatch/user facility reporting under 21 CFR Part 803, our internal safety event system, the manufacturer complaint, and Joint Commission sentinel event policy if relevant, with which apply depending on facts I must confirm, (4) open questions for the risk manager. Do not reach conclusions about fault or negligence.
prompts.caution: Reporting determinations belong to risk management and legal; regulatory thresholds must be checked against current FDA rules.

prompts.title: Credentialing and proctoring pathway
prompts.task: Draft a robotic privileging pathway for surgeons and bedside staff
prompts.prompt: Help me draft a credentialing and competency pathway for our robotic program on [SYSTEM MODEL(S)]. Roles: console surgeons (new-to-robotics and experienced transfers), first assists, scrub and circulating nurses. Our medical staff bylaws require [REQUIREMENTS]. Reference widely used elements: vendor online modules and simulator scores, dry/wet lab, proctored cases, case-volume maintenance, and published society guidance (e.g., SAGES, AORN) where applicable. Output: a tiered table per role with requirements, evidence documents, who signs off, and recertification cadence, plus a separate list of decisions our credentials committee must make. Flag where professional guidance is inconsistent or not standardized.
prompts.caution: Privileging is a medical staff decision; verify current society guidance rather than relying on summaries.

prompts.title: Patient-facing robotic surgery explainer
prompts.task: Write plain-language patient education about robot-assisted surgery
prompts.prompt: Write a patient handout for people scheduled for robot-assisted [PROCEDURE] at our hospital. Reading level: 6th to 8th grade; also provide a one-paragraph version for [LANGUAGE] translation review. Explain that the surgeon controls the robot at all times, what the patient may notice (small incisions, positioning, recovery expectations per [SURGEON'S STANDARD RECOVERY NOTES]), and what questions to ask the surgeon, including the surgeon's experience, possible conversion to open or laparoscopic surgery, and alternatives. Avoid marketing claims and do not state outcome superiority unless I supply the evidence: [EVIDENCE OR 'NONE']. Format: headings, short bullets, under 400 words.
prompts.caution: Have the surgeon and patient education committee approve; this does not replace informed consent.

prompts.title: Program expansion and capital plan
prompts.task: Evaluate adding a system, platform, or telesurgery capability
prompts.prompt: You are advising a hospital robotics committee on whether to [ADD A SECOND SYSTEM / ADD A NEW PLATFORM SUCH AS (MODEL) / PILOT REMOTE PROCTORING OR TELESURGERY]. Inputs: current volume and utilization [DATA], projected demand by service [PROJECTIONS], capital and service contract quotes [QUOTES], staffing [STAFF], network infrastructure [IT DETAILS]. Produce a decision memo: options compared in a table (cost, volume needed to break even, training burden, multi-platform complexity, regulatory status of the specific indication), risks, and a phased implementation plan. For telesurgery, explicitly flag unsettled issues: FDA clearance for remote use, cross-state licensure, latency and failover requirements, liability and cybersecurity.
prompts.caution: Check each device's actual FDA clearance and indications; telesurgery regulation is still forming.

prompts.title: Coordinator upskilling plan
prompts.task: Build a learning plan for a new or growing coordinator role
prompts.prompt: I am a [BACKGROUND, e.g., OR nurse / surgical tech / biomed] moving into a surgical robot coordinator role at a [HOSPITAL SIZE] program running [SYSTEMS]. Build a 90-day learning plan covering: system architecture and IFU basics, instrument life and reprocessing, IEC 80601-2-77 and ISO 14971 concepts at a user level, FDA MAUDE searching for our devices, data analytics for OR efficiency, cybersecurity basics for networked devices (FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance, hospital IT segmentation), and stakeholder management. For each week give objectives, specific resources types (vendor training, standards, society guidance), a practical exercise, and a self-check question. Mark items where I should verify that a resource is current.
prompts.caution: Confirm standards versions and vendor training requirements; summaries may be outdated.
